Press Release

SEC Charges Founder of American Bitcoin Academy Online Crypto Course with Fraud Targeting Students

Defendant claimed his hedge fund would use sophisticated tools like artificial intelligence to generate returns

For Immediate Release

2024-13

Washington D.C., 2024-02-02 —

The Securities and Exchange Commission announced that Brian Sewell and Rockwell Capital Management agreed to settle fraud charges in connection with a scheme targeting students in the American Bitcoin Academy online crypto trading course. The alleged scheme cost 15 students $1.2 million.

From early 2018 to mid-2019, Sewell encouraged students to invest in a hedge fund he claimed would use artificial intelligence and crypto asset trading strategies.

The complaint alleges he received approximately $1.2 million but never launched the fund or executed the advertised strategies, instead holding the invested money in bitcoin. The bitcoin was later stolen when his digital wallet was hacked.

The defendants consented to injunctive relief. Rockwell Capital Management agreed to pay disgorgement and prejudgment interest, and Sewell agreed to a civil penalty, subject to court approval.
